result.summary: Re-gate of my own original Step 2c FAIL (handoffs/WF02-REQ-023/step-02c-security-reviewer.json), against BACKEND-DEV's rework (commit 3191bdc) and REVIEWER's independent re-gate PASS (step-02b-reviewer-regate.json). Read `git show 3191bdc` in full myself, then read the resulting code directly (apps/bot/src/handlers/withdraw.ts lines 150-227, apps/bot/src/domain/user.ts lines 140-179) rather than trusting either producer's summary. 1. Fix genuinely closes the original S10 finding, scoped correctly. `getUserForNotificationById` (domain/user.ts:162-179) now projects `blocked: users.blocked` alongside tgId/lang/chapterDefaultLang -- confirmed by reading the SELECT projection directly, not the diff hunk in isolation. `sendPromotionNotification` (handlers/withdraw.ts:178-227) adds `if (promotedUser.blocked) { return; }` at line 197-199, immediately after the pre-existing null-tgId guard (line 189-191) and strictly before resolveLang/catalog lookup/eventTitle-dateTime composition/ctx.api.sendMessage (lines 200-226). This is a true short-circuit, confirmed by reading the function's full control flow top to bottom, not inferred from the diff's line numbers alone. `staff.ts`'s pre-existing, structurally-identical gap remains correctly out of this diff's scope -- confirmed `git show 3191bdc --stat` touches only domain/user.ts, handlers/withdraw.ts, handlers/withdraw.test.ts, docs/agents/design/REQ-023.md, and its own handoff bookkeeping file; staff.ts does not appear. ISS-0020.yaml (docs/issues/ISS-0020.yaml) correctly records it as MAJOR, open, affected_files naming staff.ts/domain/user.ts/REQ-023.md, discovered_by REVIEWER during the Step 2b re-gate -- read the file directly, content matches the handoff's description with no drift. 2. Re-verified the promotion-vs-notification split, the actual point of S10's intent (suppress SENDS, not suppress the underlying state change). Traced the call site: handlers/withdraw.ts's confirm handler invokes withdrawRegistration first, which commits admission/audit/seat-freeing inside promoteFromWaitlistIfEligible's transaction (registration.ts, untouched by this commit -- confirmed via `git show 3191bdc --stat` showing zero changes to registration.ts/registration.db.test.ts/event.ts, the exact files verified for S7/S8/S9/T-24h-halt at the original full pass); sendPromotionNotification is called only afterward, on outcome.promotion.kind === 'promoted'. The blocked-skip guard lives entirely inside sendPromotionNotification, a function with no DB-write capability of its own (it only reads via getUserForNotificationById/getEventIdForRegistration/getEventByIdWithChapterTimezone and sends via ctx.api.sendMessage) -- it structurally cannot roll back or alter anything already committed. Re-ran BACKEND-DEV's new test myself: `TEST_DATABASE_URL=postgres://bot:bot@localhost:55432/bot npx vitest run apps/bot/src/handlers/withdraw.test.ts -t "S10 rework" --reporter=verbose` -> 1 passed, 5 correctly skipped (real DB path taken, not the dbAvailable-false skip branch) -- confirms for a blocked promoted person: admission becomes 'admitted' with a fresh 64-hex qrToken, exactly one AuditLog row exists for that registration, and captured Telegram calls are exactly [answerCallbackQuery, sendMessage-to-withdrawer] with zero sendMessage to the blocked person's chat_id. This matches S10's actual intent precisely: the state change (admission/audit/seat-freeing) is unaffected; only the send is withheld. I did not need to construct a further negative variant beyond REVIEWER's independently-constructed second one (blocked-candidate-first-in-waitlist-order, reported in step-02b-reviewer-regate.json) -- that variant already answers the specific question of whether blocked status could leak into promotion eligibility or queue order (it does not: the blocked candidate is still the one legitimately promoted when they are earliest in line), which is exactly the re-verification this re-gate's task step 3 calls for. Read that report's reasoning and evidence directly rather than accepting its PASS verdict at face value; the trace is sound and the described test would produce the claimed result given the code as read. 3. No new security concern introduced by the fix itself. The guard is `if (promotedUser.blocked) { return; }` -- a plain boolean branch on server-side data already fetched in the same query as tgId/lang (no additional query, no additional round-trip whose timing could differ observably). It introduces no new external-facing signal: the only observable effect of the branch is the ABSENCE of a Telegram message to the promoted person, which is not visible to any other party (not the withdrawer, who only ever sees their own confirmedReply; not the promoted person, who by definition receives nothing either way they can compare against). No error message, log line, or audit payload field is added or changed by this commit that could disclose `blocked` status to anyone -- confirmed by reading the diff's full content (grep for console/log calls in the changed hunks: zero). No timing side-channel: the skip returns before any Telegram API call, network I/O, or additional DB read that a non-blocked path performs, so the two paths differ in wall-clock time in the same direction and for the same structural reason every early-return guard in this codebase already does (e.g. the pre-existing null-tgId guard immediately above it) -- not a new class of behavior. Confirmed no code path anywhere reads `promotedUser.blocked` and reflects it back into a reply, log, or audit payload; grepped the diff's three touched source files for `blocked` -- exactly two occurrences, both in domain/user.ts's interface/select and withdraw.ts's guard, none in any string composition or writeAuditLog call. 4. Scope re-verified myself, independent of both prior reports. `git diff eb3a9a5..a7c58e0 --name-only` (the range between REVIEWER's re-gate and the current HEAD) shows only docs/issues/ISS-0020.yaml -- the issue-filing commit, unrelated to the fix itself and correctly out of scope for this gate (it documents a pre-existing, different file's gap). `git show 3191bdc --name-only` confirms the fix commit itself touches exactly: apps/bot/src/domain/user.ts, apps/bot/src/handlers/withdraw.test.ts, apps/bot/src/handlers/withdraw.ts, docs/agents/design/REQ-023.md, and handoffs/WF02-REQ-023/step-02-backend-dev-rework1.json -- matching this task's expected scope list exactly, nothing more. registration.ts, registration.db.test.ts, event.ts, i18n/*, and every other file verified at my original full S1-S14 pass (commit f1dae51) are untouched since that pass, confirmed via the same `git show --stat`. 5. Re-ran the full verification suite myself, real output (see evidence.commands): `npm run lint` -> exit 0, 0 errors, same 2 pre-existing unrelated apps/web LCP warnings. `npm run build` -> exit 0, both workspaces (Next.js build + apps/bot tsc) clean. `npx vitest run --no-file-parallelism` (repo root, scratch Postgres bot-postgres-1 already running) -> 17 files / 212 tests passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped -- matches both prior reports' counts exactly, independently re-run by me a third time. `npx vitest run apps/bot/src/handlers/withdraw.test.ts -t "S10 rework" --reporter=verbose` -> 1 passed (the specific S10 negative case), 5 correctly skipped as unrelated tests in the same file (not because the DB was unavailable -- confirmed by the S10 test itself running to completion against real Postgres in 156ms). Verdict: PASS. The original S10 FAIL is closed for the code path it was raised against (sendPromotionNotification). No new concern introduced by the fix. Scope is exactly the expected file set plus the correctly-out-of-scope ISS-0020.yaml filing. All S1-S14 items I re-derived at the original full pass (S7/S8/S9/T-24h-halt/S3-cross-leak/S4-token/S11-no-PII-in-logs) are unaffected, since none of their supporting files changed in this rework.
